requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`. Each obligation maps to at least one marked test with assertions.

**Terms referenced by the subject, a contributed source, or an acknowledgment must each contribute a complete declaration.**
- Subject: `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` has the subject cite `terms.unit`. It asserts that exactly two definition inputs reach the mandatory set.
- Contributed source: `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms]` has a staged source reference `terms.ready`. It asserts that the definition appears in the mandatory inputs. It also asserts that the harness reports an error when the terms file is unstaged.
- Acknowledgment: `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[acknowledgment_only_terms_are_supplied_and_validated_without_implementation_reads]` uses a `{fixme}` body that references `terms.boundary`. The prompt contains the text of the definitions `terms.boundary` and `terms.unit`. The prompt does not contain the implementation body, and no outline inputs are created. The test also checks that the record validates, that a change to `terms.unit` is detected, and that a missing definition input is reported.
- Cited requirements and examples are not a separate input class. `definition_inputs` computes definitions over the whole mandatory input list in one pass, so the tested paths exercise the same code.

**Complete fenced declaration including the phrase option.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission]` asserts that each recorded definition's text starts with `:::{definition}` and that its second line starts with `:phrase: `.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` asserts the `:phrase: value` line on a read.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` asserts the full four-line declaration text.

**Transitive, without duplicates, and without nontermination on cycles.**
- In the bundle test, `terms.unit` and `terms.value` reference each other, so the definitions form a cycle. The test asserts that exactly two definitions are supplied, so each appears once and the traversal terminates.
- The `mod.rs` test also uses a cycle. It asserts the exact list `["terms.unit","terms.value"]`, which is the transitive set once each.
- The redaction test checks transitive inclusion of `terms.base` through `terms.value`.
- The acknowledgment test checks that `terms.unit` is reached through `terms.boundary`.

**A read that introduces a terminology dependency.**
- `definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission` runs `assess` with a provider that reads `src/lib.rs`.
  - The first request does not contain "A unit of".
  - The second request does, so the definitions were delivered before the submission.
  - The transitive set is recorded once each in the evidence inputs.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` and the paging test `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]` cover item reads and line-range reads, including paged delivery.
  - Item reads: definitions arrive with the read and are recorded.
  - Line-range reads: the same definitions arrive and are recorded.
  - Paged delivery: a page carries exactly its own definitions.

No obligations are delegated to other requirements here, and there are no acknowledgments.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
:::{req} fixme_inputs
For a requirement or example assessment, the initial request MUST include every
valid named `{fixme}` reference to the subject found under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except a reference inside one of
the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, in this
form:
```text
Acknowledgment {
file: String,
item: String,
body: String,
issues: Array<{ reference: String, state: "open" | "closed" }>,
`file` and `item` MUST locate the containing source by project-relative path and
outline selector, using `<root>` for a whole file. `body` MUST contain the
reference's complete fenced commentary without its fences or source-comment
delimiters, including its option lines, redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. `issues` MUST give every distinct issue
its `:github:` lines name, in their order, with state supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`. Acknowledgments MUST be ordered by
file and position in the file and MUST carry no line numbers or containing
implementation source.
The locations and bodies MUST be protected against staleness by the reference-set
digest under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`; the acknowledgment MUST NOT
create an outline input merely to cover its containing source. Actual reads of
that source MUST still be recorded under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Sources MUST satisfy
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; an inaccessible acknowledgment
MUST be reported before inference.
Terminology definitions referenced by an acknowledgment's body MUST contribute
their complete, transitive declarations to the mandatory input set under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` and MUST be recorded as
definition inputs. Only the acknowledgment's body MUST contribute these
dependencies; its containing implementation source MUST NOT be supplied merely
to discover them.
